history.origins: Omben is the Indonesian/Javanese variant of the quartet-collection family that includes Go Fish and Authors. The name 'drink' may refer to the penalty of drawing when the opponent has no card of the requested rank.
timeline: Quartet games originated mid-19th century with special packs (Happy Families, Authors).
Omben/Minuman documented as the Indonesian adaptation, best for two players.
Present: Played in Indonesia as a children's and family game.
history.cultural: A traditional Indonesian children's and family card game, especially in Java.
history.evolution: Differs from standard Go Fish: two players only, asker continues drawing until finding the requested rank when opponent has none (the 'drink'), and first to empty hand wins (not most books).

setup.players: Two players. Omben (Indonesian Go Fish) is played by exactly two players; each begins with 4 or 5 cards by agreement drawn from a 52-card pack, and the remainder forms the face-down stock.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 4 or 5 cards (by agreement). Remaining cards form a face-down stock.

rules.objective: Be the first to get rid of all your cards by forming and discarding books (four of a kind).
rules.gameplay: 1. Players take turns asking the opponent for a specific rank (e.g. 8 or king). 2. The asker must hold at least one card of that rank. 3. If the opponent has cards of that rank, they give all of them to the asker. 4. If the opponent has none, the asker 'drinks': draw from the stock until finding a card of the requested rank. 5. Whenever a player has four of a kind, they discard it face up. 6. Winner is the first to empty their hand. If the stock runs out, the player with fewer cards wins. 7. Turns alternate regardless of whether the request was successful.
keyRules: Must hold at least one card of the rank you ask for.
Opponent gives all cards of that rank if they have any.
If opponent has none, asker draws until finding one (the 'drink').
Four of a kind must be discarded immediately.
First to empty hand wins; if stock exhausted, fewer cards wins.

strategy.basic: Ask for ranks you already have to complete books. Ask for high-frequency ranks (middle cards) early.
strategy.intermediate: Track what the opponent has asked for and what you have givenâ€”this reveals their books. Avoid giving cards that complete their four of a kind if you can delay.
strategy.advanced: Memory of discards and requests is key. If opponent repeatedly asks for a rank, they are close to a book.
tips: The 'drink' penalty can be severe if you ask for a rare rank.
With 4 cards each, the game is very short; 5 cards each gives more scope.
